content.rendered:
In early 1979, Bruce had a vision for a song.

He didn’t have much in the way of lyrics yet, but he had a hook, a theme, and a basic melody. (And if you listen closely to this home demo recording, you’ll hear him note that the song calls for a “Bennie and the Jets-type rhythm.”

It might seem like nothing every came of “Baby Don’t Go,” but listen again–there’s something vaguely familiar about the feel of the song, and the few lines that aren’t bluffed seem like they share some DNA with one of Bruce’s contemporary songs as well.

Compare:

Now maybe I’m not the kind of man who you want
Maybe I can’t deliver to you all the things you so desire

with:

Well now you say you’ve found another man who does things to you that I can’t

Did “Baby Don’t Go” ultimately lead Bruce to “Fade Away?” I can’t say with conviction, but there are certainly some similarities, and Bruce’s first take of “Fade Away” came shortly after his last recorded attempt at “Baby Don’t Go” (this time with a more up-tempo accompaniment).

Early ancestor or not, “Baby Don’t Go” is at least a fascinating inside look at the songwriting process that would shortly lead Bruce to some of his best River-era songs.

Baby Don’t Go
Recorded: March-April 1979 (demo)
Never released
Never performed

© December 10, 2019

excerpt.rendered: Listen in on an abandoned River-era demo that might have been an early ancestor of “Fade Away.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Fade Away
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Fade Away" is a young man's "Back in Your Arms," a Danny Federici-powered cry of anguish over lost love. It's beautiful and perfect--Bruce's songwriting at its best.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Take ‘Em as They Come
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A classic Springsteen formula--dark lyrics paired with a power pop melody--results in a shoulda-been new wave classic. Insights and great performances inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: All the Way Home
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A tale of two versions of the same song. One ranks near the top of Bruce's catalog, the other near the bottom. Find out which is which (and why) inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: Fade to Black
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: This Nebraska-era demo uses cinematic vocabulary to devastating effect.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Jackson Cage
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "Jackson Cage" is a case of a theme in search of a song. It took a while for Bruce to find it, but find it he did. Let's trace this underrated song's winding path inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Roll of the Dice: The Brokenhearted
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: "The Brokenhearted" is Roy Orbison meets The Drifters, and 1977 Bruce meets 2010 Bruce. The style mash-up works, the vocal graft not so much.
